phases.message: I'm Nell Harrowgate. First, at Royaltyline, read the rules, every unmatched recording on both pages, and the works already registered. Don't register anything yet: I'll send you to my distributor, my rights desk and my papers next.
This is my distributor. Read my whole catalogue: every release with its recording code, who is credited as writer and where it streams.
This is my performing-rights desk. Read my works and my latest statement.
These are my papers. Read every split sheet and note.

Back at Royaltyline. Register each song whose royalties are sitting unmatched and that I own a share of, at my own share only, with its recording code, my IPI and its ISWC. Leave alone what has no money waiting here, what isn't mine to register, and what is already done. Then tell me what you registered, the shares, and what you left alone and why.

tools.description: Every unmatched recording the collective holds royalties for: id, title, artist, ISRC, accrued dollars and first usage month. Eight a page; ask for the next with page (1 or 2).

tools.description: One unmatched recording in full, by id (UM-nn).

tools.name: register_work
tools.description: Register one musical work with the collective, by the ISRC of its recording in the unmatched list (isrc), the work's title (title), the writer (writer), her IPI (writer_ipi), the share of the work she owns and registers, in percent (share_pct), and the work's ISWC (iswc). Nell signs the registration.

rules.text: Royaltyline, the collective's member hub. Friday 9 October 2026. Topics: scope, holding, registration, shares, administered. Royaltyline holds the mechanical royalties that digital services owe for recordings it cannot yet match to a work, and pays them out once the work is registered and matched.

Friday 9 October 2026. The blanket licence (17 U.S.C. 115(d)) covers mechanical royalties for digital uses in the United States only: streams and downloads here. Performance royalties are paid through a performing rights organisation, and the money earned by a sound recording through its distributor. Neither is claimed from Royaltyline, and Royaltyline holds nothing for either.

Friday 9 October 2026. Unmatched accrued royalties are held for at least 3 years (115(d)(3)(H)) and then distributed by market share to publishers and self-administered writers (115(d)(3)(J)). Royaltyline's first distribution is in April 2027 and starts with the usage of January 2021. What is still unmatched then is shared out by market share, not paid to the writers of those songs.

Friday 9 October 2026. A work registration carries the title, each writer with his or her share, and where known the writer's IPI, the work's ISWC and the recordings, by ISRC, that belong to it. Only the title and one writer are required; the recording is what matches an unmatched royalty. Register a song whose recording is in the unmatched list.

Friday 9 October 2026. The shares of a work add up to 100 percent. A writer registers only the share she owns, not a co-writer's share and not the whole work. Each co-writer, or the publisher or administrator who represents him or her, registers that writer's own share.

Friday 9 October 2026. A share that a publisher or administrator administers is registered by that publisher or administrator, who collects it. A self-administered writer registers her own share herself, as her own publisher. A recording is matched by its ISRC and never by its title: two different songs can share a title.
